Tom — thanks for the note and great to meet the Amaya team today. Quick recap and next steps below.

Post-call recap (high level):
- SOC 2: Redwood has completed SOC 2 Type I and is currently undergoing the Type II audit; expected completion Q2 2026. We can share the SOC 2 Type I report and our control matrix now.
- GDPR/HIPAA: We support GDPR controls (data subject requests, processor agreements). For HIPAA, we can sign a BAA for covered deployments — please confirm the scope of PHI in your use case and we’ll have our legal/security team start the BAA template.
- Vendor questionnaire: thanks for the file — looping in Neha (security/compliance) to take point on the questionnaire and Rishi for retention/backups specifics.
- Data retention/deletion SLAs & logs: High-level answers below; Neha and Rishi will provide the detailed breakdown and any supporting artifacts.

Immediate answers (summary):
- Deletion SLA: For hosted API customers, primary customer data (user-generated content and model inputs) is removed within 30 days of a verified deletion request.
- Backups: Application-level backups follow a 30-day rolling snapshot policy with isolated cold storage snapshots retained up to 365 days for disaster recovery — deletion of customer data from backups can take longer due to snapshot schedules; Neha will provide exact timelines and options for accelerated purge for enterprise contracts.
- Logs: Default retention is 90 days for request/application logs and 365 days for audit/security logs. We offer configurable retention windows for enterprise customers and can shorten retention on request as part of contract terms.

Attachments: I’m attaching a short SOC summary and we’ve uploaded your questionnaire to our secure S3 intake for Neha to populate.

Next steps:
1) Neha to start the vendor questionnaire responses and share a draft via the Drive link.
2) Rishi to confirm exact backup snapshot cadence and the technical process for purging data from backups, and to provide a short note for the questionnaire.
3) If Amaya requires a BAA, please confirm scope and we’ll route to legal.

Target: initial questionnaire responses + backup/purge note by Thu 26 Mar.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

Hi Marissa / Tom — thanks for the ping. I pulled together the initial questionnaire responses and the retention/purge details below. Attaching the SOC Type I report and a short control matrix for Amaya’s review.

Vendor questionnaire: I uploaded our responses to the Drive folder you shared and attached a copy here for reference. I’ve flagged a few items that need legal input (BAA language) — noted inline.

Key retention/purge details (technical + SLA):
- Primary customer data (model inputs / generated outputs): Standard deletion SLA is 30 days from verified request. For enterprise contracts, we can negotiate shorter windows or expedited purge procedures (e.g., prioritized pipeline to remove data from hot storage within 48 hours and from snapshots within 7-30 days depending on snapshot cadence).
- Backups / snapshots:
  - Snapshot cadence: daily application snapshots retained for 30 days (rolling).
  - Weekly full snapshots moved to cold storage and retained up to 365 days for DR; by default these are purged on a rolling 365-day policy.
  - Purging from backups: automated snapshot pruning removes snapshots per retention schedule. For deletion requests, we can run an enterprise purge that: 1) identifies snapshots containing affected objects, 2) constructs new snapshots excluding those objects where feasible, and 3) marks older snapshots for expedited deletion. Typical expedited purge timelines are 7-30 days depending on volume; we can include a contractual SLA for <30 day purge for enterprise customers.
- Logs:
  - Request/application logs: default 90 days retention (stored in encrypted logging buckets).
  - Audit/security logs: default 365 days retention.
  - We can configure shorter retention per contract and support export or deletion on request.
- GDPR / DSARs: We support data subject access and deletion requests; deletion follows the same pipeline as above with the 30-day default SLA unless otherwise contracted.

Attachments provided: Redwood_SOC2_TypeI_2026.pdf, Redwood_Control_Matrix_2026.xlsx, Questionnaire_Responses_Amaya.xlsx

- If Amaya wants an accelerated backup purge SLA, we can include language in the contract and scope an implementation plan (Rishi + infra will own the technical work).

Thanks,
